we propose a novel end-to-end handwriting model, that does not require any pre-processing or segmentation.
we present an attention-based end-to-end model for handwriting recognition, and the model does not require any prior segmentation into lines.

In summary, our research is concerned with

the following contributions: (1) we propose an end-to-end attention-based handwriting recognition system, (2) we propose an attention-based multi-dimensional LSTM network to handle covert and overt attention for handwriting, (3) we show that our system outperforms previous approaches, and (4) we show that the system can be used in an online setting, i.e. it is capable of predicting the next character in real time.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed model can be considered as a first attempt to end-to-end handwritten paragraph recognition.
the proposed model is able to outperform the state of the art by a large margin.
our model achieves the best results on the IAM database for a single model, without using a segmentation step.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are now able to read handwritten paragraphs without any prior segmentation into lines or words.
we are able to read a handwritten text with the accuracy of 82% without any prior segmentation of the input image.
we are able to achieve 3% absolute improvement over the state-of-the-art results for end-to-end paragraph transcription.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multi-dimensional attention mechanism is able to learn the paragraph structure and perform a segmentation into lines, words, and characters.
the multi-line attention is a promising approach for end-to-end transcription of handwriting, which does not require any prior segmentation into lines.
end-to-end models are feasible for handwriting recognition and can be used to solve the segmentation problem.
